I will still do wheat-maize on all 5.5 mu, same as before. On my land, if I save too much on fertilizer, the ears get small and the grain does not fill well, so I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield. I have well irrigation, so I can push yield more steadily than people who wait only for rain. What I do is mostly based on what has worked here in Quzhou these years and what I see on nearby fields that harvest well. For wheat, I will keep fertilizer a little heavier because wheat here responds clearly to water and fertilizer, and I will irrigate at the key times. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed, give enough nitrogen, and keep one or two irrigations ready depending on rain. My farm is only 5.5 mu, so I can still manage it carefully myself and with family help, but cash is not loose, so I will not chase fancy inputs. I will use improved seed where it pays, keep pesticide sprays to the usual key timings, and stay close to the pattern that has given stable harvests.
